S2. MATERIAL FINDING 1: choosing close-and-recap while resuming the ORIGINAL campaign drops character custody for the replacement session, so ordinary subsequent progress cannot sync/release and the next resume misclassifies it as stale. Authority: parent acceptance criterion 2 (legitimate crash/resume of the original preserves valid unsynchronized progress and can sync/release normally), ADR 0012 continuing-character ownership through the whole session and release carrying progress forward, ADR 0020 section 3 identity/ownership/persistence integrity. This is entirely sequential, uses one physical campaign database and its real writer lock, and needs no second campaign or concurrent writer.

Mechanism/locations: packages/cli/src/play.ts:85 acquires character custody BEFORE launch at :88 and enters turnLoop at :89 without reacquiring it. packages/cli/src/playSession.ts:131-139 handles close/c by running gracefulClose and then startNewSession. gracefulClose releases every character at packages/cli/src/playClose.ts:276. Consequently the replacement session plays with no custody row. Its final /quit reaches syncBackLocked at packages/core/src/character/characterCustody.ts:503-511, which correctly refuses a non-holder, so registry progress stays behind. The campaign writer lock stays held throughout; that lock protects the database but does not replace character custody across campaigns. This is a pre-existing affected-path defect discovered by this requested whole-subsystem review, not a claim it was first introduced at this head.

Concrete exact-head reproducer: /tmp/pr711-single-writer-review/close-resume.test.ts:55-90. File-backed registry and original campaign, real runPlay, real acquireCampaignWriterLock, real session lifecycle and real /money command; no fake model turns or raw state corruption. Register/check out Mira, open session, gain 10 gp through adjustCharacterCurrency, close the connection without releasing custody to model a crash. Resume original path; answer close; then /money gain gp 5; then /quit. runPlay returns 0. Immediately before the new session's first input custody is null. Persisted campaign wallet is 15 gp, registry wallet remains 10 gp at revision 2, and classification is stale-copy with localRevision 2/headRevision 2. Evidence: close-close-evidence.json under that /tmp directory, including complete prompts/output; close-c-evidence.json proves the accepted c alias has the same outcome. Resuming again therefore routes valid original progress to conflict resolution; the primary catch-up option would replace the 15-gp sheet with the 10-gp head. No movement to another campaign or restore/fork occurred.

Sibling/state variation: the same probe with resume retains custody and releases all 15 gp, with resumable classification afterward (close-resume-evidence.json). Existing runDemo's close branch reacquires custody AFTER launch (play.ts:161-167), so it also releases 15 gp correctly (close-demo-close-evidence.json). The lost-custody window affects every already-linked party character released by close-and-recap, not only currency or pc-1. The already disclosed eshyra-nwu2 concerns the stale-release no-op message; this finding is the independently demonstrated missing ownership/reacquisition that creates the no-op and strands valid progress, rather than a request for that message change.

Owner/closure: CLI play/session lifecycle in this scope. Preserve or re-establish custody across the in-process close-and-start-new transition BEFORE new gameplay, retaining pre-launch stale/held-elsewhere fail-closed checks. Do not simply remove the core holder guard or add concurrent-writer CAS. Proportionate permanent evidence: one generalized session-rollover invariant covering normal resume and close/c (plus the demo sibling), asserting linked characters hold custody throughout subsequent play, legitimate state changes reach the registry on final exit, and original resume does not become stale. These exact 10/5-gp fixtures and /tmp probe are not required to become permanent. The lifecycle repair is material and requires fresh full review.

S4. NON-MATERIAL passing observation: writer-lock mechanism and complete CLI entrypoint inventory match the accepted ADR scope. Independently enumerated index.ts dispatch, every campaign openDb/openDatabase site, and session consumers: play/resume/ESHYRA_DB_PATH (play.ts:48-59, before open/initSchema), demo (play.ts:113-124), new and first-campaign picker creation (campaigns.ts:66-85), checkpoint restore/fork source campaign (checkpoints.ts:42-59 and :157/:200). Play/demo hold the lock across character setup, launch, all turns, /rules, /addpc, /switch, /levelup, /money, /dispute, catch-up/fork, character release, arc rollup, and graceful-close checkpoint. There is no separate rules or checkpoint-create command. Source checkpoint history and fork branch mutation follow the ADR scope; destinations are new-only atomic no-clobber publication, never replacement of an existing active campaign.

Read-only/no campaign lock: adventures, checkpoint list, campaigns list/add/remove/rename (registry JSON only), usage, chronicle, create-character and fork-character (character registry only), banner and dolt install. Adventures opens no migration or state mutation; registry/draft/diagnostics writers operate on their own stores. lock-lifecycle.test.ts runs real adventures and checkpoint list while the writer is held, plus all four campaigns-registry commands with a lock-acquisition sentinel, and verifies the complete serialized campaign remains identical. File and directory symlink aliases, relative path aliases, and absent databases under symlinked directories share the lock.

Core lock uses timeout 0, locking_mode EXCLUSIVE and held BEGIN EXCLUSIVE on the sidecar (campaignWriterLock.ts:65-87); in-process and cross-process contenders are refused. Repository child-process tests demonstrate SIGKILL releases the lock without cleanup. Acquisition failures close their connection; success wrappers enclose database opening and the full async command in finally, and nested database finally blocks do not bypass release. Targeted probes verify release after play/demo open errors, new/picker creation errors, checkpoint restore/fork operation failures, and normal close/resume exits. This is OS custody, with no PID/stale-lock scheme. Advisory cooperation, harmless persistent sidecars and filesystems lacking working locks are honestly disclosed.
